newsitem.title: USA: Northwest U.S. utilities still battling outages.
newsitem.headline: Northwest U.S. utilities still battling outages.

text.p: Electric utilities in the Pacific Northwest and northern California continued to battle scattered power line outages in the wake of recent winter storms, utility sources said Monday.
Puget Sound Power and Light Co, based in Bellevue, Washington, said it had 63,765 customers without power as of Monday morning.
The number is down from a peak of more than 250,000 on Friday, said spokeswoman Betty Werblun.
"This is our third storm since Thursday," she noted. "The rain is causing flooding and ground instability, which could be a problem if the wind comes up."
Werblun said no major power lines were out, with Puget Power "down to (repairing) the nitty gritty distribution lines."
Portland General Electric said about 5,000 of its customers were without power, down from a peak of around 130,000 on Friday.
"We are continuing to chip away at it," said Portland General spokeswoman Vicky Rocker. "We are down to tap lines now."

San Francisco-based Pacific Gas and Electric Co, which saw outages peak near 100,000 on Sunday, said about 2,000 customers in its northern and central California service territory were without power as of Monday morning.
"The winds are starting to kick in again, so the numbers are back from 1,400 earlier," said PG&E spokesman Cory Warren.
He noted most of the outages have been in coastal areas, where falling trees have knocked down local power lines.
Warren said the storm did not cause any of PG&E's power plants to trip off nor were any major transmission lines affected.

The California utility does expect recent heavy snowfall to result in healthy hydroelectric generation from its Sierra Nevada projects next spring, but said there was no significant impact in the near term.
